repositories.name: Aider
repositories.citation: [1] Aider-AI. "Aider - AI pair programming in your terminal." GitHub, v0.86.0 (Aug 2025). https://github.com/Aider-AI/aider
key_features: Automatic codebase mapping for large projects
84.9% correctness on polyglot benchmarks with o3-pro
repositories.architecture: Terminal-first tool that maintains codebase context through mapping. Uses LLM APIs to generate code changes and automatically commits with git. Works with any LLM provider including local models.
repositories.pricing: Open source (Apache 2.0), LLM API costs apply
repositories.threat_rationale: Extremely popular (38k+ stars), CLI-first like SkillRunner, supports local LLMs, strong Git integration, and excellent benchmark performance. Direct competitor in the terminal-based AI coding space.

repositories.name: Cline (formerly Claude Dev)
repositories.citation: [2] Cline. "Cline - Autonomous coding agent right in your IDE." VS Code Marketplace, 2025. https://github.com/cline/cline
key_features: Autonomous coding agent in VS Code
Browser automation via Claude Computer Use
Multi-provider support (OpenRouter, Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, AWS, Azure)
Cost tracking per task and request
repositories.architecture: VS Code extension with human-in-the-loop approval system. Integrates deeply with IDE features and provides autonomous multi-file editing capabilities. Uses MCP for extensible tool integration.
repositories.pricing: Free extension (Apache 2.0), LLM API costs apply
repositories.usage_example: Install extension, configure API key, use @commands in chat to interact with codebase
limitations: Can be expensive with frontier models
repositories.threat_rationale: Most popular VS Code extension (54k stars, 4M+ installs) with cost tracking feature. However, it's IDE-locked and not CLI-based like SkillRunner. Complements rather than directly competes.

repositories.name: Cursor
repositories.citation: [3] Cursor. "Cursor - The best way to code with AI." Cursor AI, 2025. https://cursor.com/
repositories.architecture: Proprietary VS Code fork with custom AI models and multi-agent orchestration. Tightly integrated IDE experience with both autocomplete and agentic capabilities.
repositories.usage_example: Install Cursor app, use Cmd+K for inline edits or Cmd+L for chat
repositories.threat_rationale: Highly polished commercial product with strong market presence. However, it's closed source, expensive, and IDE-only. Different target audience than SkillRunner (GUI vs CLI).

repositories.name: Mentat
repositories.citation: [4] AbanteAI. "Mentat - The AI Coding Assistant." GitHub, 2025. https://github.com/AbanteAI/archive-old-cli-mentat
repositories.architecture: Originally a CLI tool for coordinated multi-file edits. Now transitioned to a GitHub bot service (mentat.ai) for pull request automation.
repositories.pricing: Open source (MIT), LLM API costs apply
repositories.usage_example: Archived CLI version no longer recommended. New version is GitHub bot integration.
repositories.threat_rationale: Original CLI tool archived and team pivoted to GitHub bot. No longer actively competing in the CLI coding assistant space.

repositories.name: GPT-Engineer
repositories.citation: [5] AntonOsika. "GPT-Engineer - CLI platform to experiment with codegen." GitHub, v0.3.1 (Jun 2024). https://github.com/AntonOsika/gpt-engineer
key_features: New code and improve existing code modes
repositories.architecture: Simple CLI that generates entire codebases from prompts. Uses planning step to create shared dependencies, then generates all files. Customizable through preprompts that define agent behavior.
repositories.threat_rationale: Popular for initial code generation (55k stars) but limited iteration capabilities. Team pivoted to commercial lovable.dev. More of a code scaffolding tool than workflow orchestrator.

repositories.name: Sweep AI
repositories.citation: [6] Sweep AI. "Sweep - AI-powered junior developer for GitHub." GitHub, 2025. https://github.com/sweepai/sweep
repositories.architecture: GitHub App that monitors issues with 'Sweep:' prefix and automatically generates pull requests. Uses codebase analysis to determine changes needed and creates PRs with proposed solutions.
repositories.pricing: Open source (Apache 2.0), now commercial JetBrains plugin
repositories.usage_example: Install Sweep GitHub App, create issue with 'Sweep:' prefix, AI generates PR
repositories.threat_rationale: Specialized for GitHub issue → PR workflow. Team pivoted to JetBrains plugin. Not a general workflow orchestrator like SkillRunner.

repositories.name: OpenHands (formerly OpenDevin)
repositories.citation: [7] All Hands AI. "OpenHands - Open Platform for Cloud Coding Agents." GitHub, v1.0.7-cli (Nov 2025). https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands
key_features: Software Agent SDK for custom agents
Cloud deployment with integrations (Slack, Jira, Linear)
repositories.architecture: Comprehensive platform offering SDK, CLI, GUI, and cloud deployment options. Designed for building and scaling AI coding agents from local development to enterprise production.
repositories.pricing: Open source (MIT), enterprise licensing for production use after 1 month
repositories.threat_rationale: Most popular open-source coding agent (65k+ stars), offers CLI interface, local-first capable, and actively maintained. Comprehensive platform that can scale from local to enterprise. Direct competitor to SkillRunner.

repositories.name: Continue.dev
repositories.citation: [8] Continue. "Continue - Open-source autopilot for software development." GitHub, v1.34.0 (Dec 2025). https://github.com/continuedev/continue
key_features: Cloud agents (PR opens, schedules, custom triggers)
Custom AI assistant sharing via Continue Hub
repositories.architecture: Multi-interface platform: cloud agents for automation, CLI for terminal workflows, and IDE extensions for in-editor assistance. Hub allows sharing custom AI assistants across teams.
repositories.pricing: Open source (Apache 2.0), commercial Continue Cloud offering
repositories.usage_example: Install IDE extension or use CLI: continue agent run
limitations: CLI agents less mature than IDE features
repositories.threat_rationale: Growing rapidly (30k stars) with CLI + cloud agent capabilities. However, primarily IDE-focused with cloud dependencies. Competes in automation space but different architecture than SkillRunner.

repositories.name: Goose (by Block/Square)
repositories.citation: [9] Block. "Goose - Open source extensible AI agent." GitHub, v1.15.0 (Nov 2025). https://github.com/block/goose
repositories.architecture: Local-first agent built on Model Context Protocol (MCP) developed with Anthropic. Transforms natural language into actions across tools and services. Designed for extensibility and local operation.
repositories.threat_rationale: Backed by major fintech company (Block), local-first design, MCP integration, 22k+ stars, and production use by 5000 employees. Strong enterprise validation and similar CLI-first approach to SkillRunner.

repositories.name: Devika
repositories.citation: [10] Stition AI. "Devika - Agentic AI Software Engineer (now Opcode)." GitHub, 2025. https://github.com/stitionai/devika
key_features: Supports Claude 3, GPT-4, Gemini, Mistral, Groq
repositories.architecture: Autonomous agent that breaks down high-level objectives into steps, researches information, and writes code. Designed as open-source alternative to Devin with modular architecture for planning, research, and code generation.
repositories.threat_rationale: Popular (19k stars) but experimental and transitioning to new product (Opcode). Not production-ready. Potential future competitor but currently not a direct threat.

repositories.name: SWE-agent
repositories.citation: [11] Princeton NLP. "SWE-agent - Agent Computer Interfaces Enable Software Engineering Language Models." GitHub, v1.1.0 (May 2025). https://github.com/SWE-agent/SWE-agent
key_features: State of the art on SWE-bench
EnIGMA mode for cybersecurity CTF challenges
repositories.architecture: Academic research project focused on agent-computer interfaces for software engineering. Designed to automatically resolve GitHub issues using LLMs with specialized tooling and interfaces optimized for coding tasks.
limitations: Academic project (may have limited long-term support)
repositories.threat_rationale: Academic research project (Princeton/Stanford) with excellent benchmark results but limited scope (GitHub issue resolution). Not designed as general workflow orchestrator like SkillRunner.

repositories.name: Bolt.new (by StackBlitz)
repositories.citation: [12] StackBlitz. "Bolt.new - AI full-stack web app builder." GitHub, 2025. https://github.com/stackblitz/bolt.new
key_features: AI control over filesystem, terminal, browser
repositories.architecture: Browser-based development environment powered by WebContainers. AI has complete control over development environment including filesystem, server, package manager, and terminal. Tightly coupled with StackBlitz infrastructure.
repositories.usage_example: Visit bolt.new, describe app, AI builds and deploys it
repositories.threat_rationale: Different category - browser-based web app builder vs local CLI orchestrator. Serves rapid prototyping market. 1M+ deployments show market validation but different target audience than SkillRunner.

repositories.name: Smol Developer
repositories.citation: [13] Smol AI. "Smol Developer - Junior developer agent library." GitHub, 2025. https://github.com/smol-ai/developer
key_features: Three modes: Git repo, Library, API
repositories.architecture: Minimalist library focused on whole-program synthesis from natural language specs. Philosophy of 'simple, safe, and smol' - easy to understand and modify core codebase.
repositories.threat_rationale: Interesting minimal approach (12k stars) but alpha stage and limited to code generation. Not a workflow orchestrator. Philosophy of simplicity is appealing but lacks production features.

repositories.name: PearAI
repositories.citation: [14] PearAI. "PearAI - Open Source AI Code Editor (Fork of VSCode)." GitHub, v1.8.9 (May 2025). https://github.com/trypear/pearai-app
key_features: VS Code fork with AI integration
Fork of Continue for AI features
repositories.architecture: VS Code fork with Continue integration for AI capabilities. Emphasizes local storage and privacy while maintaining familiar IDE experience.
repositories.usage_example: Download PearAI app, configure AI provider
repositories.threat_rationale: Small community, fork of existing tools with limited differentiation. License controversy hurt adoption. Not a significant competitive threat.

repositories.name: v0.dev / v0.app (by Vercel)
repositories.citation: [15] Vercel. "v0 - AI builder for everyone." Vercel, 2025. https://v0.app/
key_features: AI app builder with UI, content, backend, logic
repositories.architecture: Commercial SaaS platform using custom composite AI architecture. Combines RAG, reasoning LLMs, and custom AutoFix model. Generates React/Next.js code with shadcn/ui and Tailwind CSS.
repositories.usage_example: Visit v0.app, describe app, iterate with AI, deploy to Vercel
repositories.threat_rationale: Commercial web app builder targeting rapid prototyping and marketing sites. Different category than CLI workflow orchestrator. Large user base but serves different use case than SkillRunner.

repositories.name: Replit Agent
repositories.citation: [16] Replit. "Replit Agent - AI app builder." Replit, 2025. https://replit.com/agent3
key_features: Full app creation from natural language
repositories.architecture: Commercial cloud-based IDE with autonomous AI agents. Agent 3 can operate continuously for extended periods, testing and refining code in reflection loops. Can spawn specialized sub-agents for workflows.
repositories.usage_example: Visit replit.com, describe app, Agent builds and deploys it
repositories.threat_rationale: Cloud-based IDE platform for beginners and rapid prototyping. Different market segment than local-first CLI orchestrators. Strong in education market but not competing directly with SkillRunner.

common_patterns: Terminal/CLI interfaces gaining popularity over IDE-only solutions
Local LLM support increasingly important for privacy and cost
Git integration essential for all coding agents
Multi-provider support (Claude, GPT, Gemini, local) becoming standard
Cost tracking still rare but increasingly requested by users
Human-in-the-loop approval remains critical safety feature
MCP (Model Context Protocol) emerging as standard for agent extensibility
Transition from autocomplete to autonomous multi-file agents
best_practices: Provide both CLI and GUI options for different workflows
Support local LLMs (Ollama, etc.) for cost-conscious users
Implement cost tracking to prevent bill shock
Use git for automatic change tracking and rollback
Make configuration simple (single YAML or JSON file)
Focus on developer experience (DX) over feature count
pitfalls: Credit/token systems without clear pricing confuse users
Experimental features in production hurt reliability
Poor license choices damage reputation (PearAI example)
Pivot away from open-source reduces trust (Sweep, Mentat)
Expensive pricing pushes users to alternatives
emerging_trends: Shift from code completion to autonomous agents (2024-2025)
Local-first tools gaining traction for privacy/cost
Academic research projects (SWE-agent) influencing production tools
Custom AI models for coding (Cursor Composer, v0 composite)
Integration of computer use capabilities (browser automation)

implementation_recommendations.scenario: Individual developer wants local-first AI coding assistant
implementation_recommendations.rationale: Both offer excellent local LLM support, CLI-first interfaces, and strong Git integration. Aider more mature, Goose backed by major company.

implementation_recommendations.scenario: Team wants IDE-integrated coding agent with cost visibility
implementation_recommendations.rationale: Only major tool with built-in cost tracking, 4M+ installs, active development, human-in-the-loop safety, and multi-provider support.

implementation_recommendations.scenario: Enterprise needs scalable agent platform with self-hosting
implementation_recommendations.rationale: Comprehensive platform with SDK, CLI, GUI, and enterprise features. 65k stars, MIT license, Kubernetes deployment, RBAC, multi-user support.
State-of-the-art benchmark results, hackable architecture, academic backing, comprehensive documentation, research-focused design.

implementation_recommendations.scenario: Startup wants rapid web app prototyping
implementation_recommendations.rationale: Browser-based, instant deployment, no setup required. Bolt for general web apps, v0 for Next.js/React focus. 1M+ deployments validate market fit.

implementation_recommendations.scenario: Developer wants workflow orchestration with cost control
implementation_recommendations.rationale: Only tool combining multi-agent orchestration, built-in cost tracking, local-first architecture, and workflow automation. Direct CLI interface with intelligent agent delegation.

popular_solutions: Cline (54k stars) - VS Code users wanting agents
controversial_topics: Cost transparency: Many tools hide LLM costs until bills arrive
Open source vs proprietary: Community prefers open-source but polished commercial tools gain traction
License changes: PearAI controversy shows importance of proper licensing
Pivot concerns: Teams pivoting from open source to commercial (Sweep, Mentat) lose community trust
IDE lock-in: Debate over standalone editors (Cursor) vs extensions (Cline)
Benchmark gaming: Questions about whether benchmark performance translates to real-world usefulness
expert_opinions: Swyx (continuous AI advocate): 'The future is autonomous agents, not autocomplete'
StackBlitz CEO on Claude 3.5: 'The enabling technology that made this product possible, period'
Block on local-first: 'Open-source AI that pays for itself through productivity gains'
YC on agent market: 'Backing experimental projects but some like PearAI face community backlash'
Academic researchers: 'Agent-computer interfaces (ACI) critical for LLM effectiveness in software engineering'

unique_differentiators: Built-in cost tracking (only Cline has this, and it's IDE-only)
Workflow automation focus (not just coding assistance)
market_gaps_addressed: No major tool combines cost tracking + orchestration + local-first
CLI tools lack orchestration capabilities (Aider, GPT-Engineer)
Orchestration tools require cloud infrastructure (OpenHands, AutoGen)
IDE tools have vendor lock-in (Cursor, Cline)
Commercial tools lack transparency (Cursor, Replit, v0.dev)
target_audiences: Cost-conscious developers tired of surprise LLM bills
Teams needing workflow automation without enterprise complexity

high_threat.reason: Popular CLI tool (38k stars), local LLM support, excellent Git integration, strong benchmark performance
high_threat.mitigation: Focus on orchestration capabilities and cost tracking which Aider lacks

high_threat.reason: Most popular agent platform (65k stars), CLI + SDK + GUI, local-first capable, comprehensive features
high_threat.mitigation: Emphasize simplicity, cost tracking, and workflow focus vs their platform complexity

high_threat.reason: Enterprise-backed (Block), local-first, MCP integration, production use by 5000 employees
high_threat.mitigation: Highlight cost tracking and multi-agent orchestration. Goose is agent library, SkillRunner is workflow orchestrator

medium_threat.reason: Most popular VS Code extension (54k stars, 4M installs), has cost tracking
medium_threat.mitigation: Different category (IDE vs CLI). Target developers wanting terminal workflows and orchestration

medium_threat.reason: Polished commercial product, custom models, strong brand
medium_threat.mitigation: Open-source vs proprietary, local-first vs cloud-dependent, transparent cost vs subscription

medium_threat.reason: Growing CLI capabilities, cloud agents, good momentum (30k stars)
medium_threat.mitigation: Focus on local-first, cost tracking, and workflow orchestration depth

low_threat: Mentat (archived CLI, pivoted to GitHub bot)
GPT-Engineer (limited to code generation, team focused on commercial product)
Sweep AI (specialized GitHub issue → PR workflow, pivoted to JetBrains)
Bolt.new (browser-based web app builder, different market)
